candidates.statement: Gateway /v1/checkout returns 502 because its downstream call to order:8000/v1/orders returns HTTP 500. Traces and logs show each checkout 502 paired with a client-side 500 from the order service, so the fault originates in the order service, not the gateway.
candidates.uncertainty: Order-service internal cause (db, payment, inventory) not observed; only gateway-side evidence available.

report.explanation: Gateway checkout 502s are consistently caused by 500 responses from the order service on /v1/orders, per correlated traces and logs. The gateway itself is healthy (readyz 200). Root cause lies in the order service; its internal failure mode is not yet observed, so the bounded candidate is the downstream HTTP 500.
missing_evidence: Order-service traces/logs for POST /v1/orders showing the internal error origin
Order-service dependency metrics (postgresql, payment, inventory) to localize the 500
